correction.text: the same shape, drawn 1111-1115 and 1140-1187; in 1116-1139 the land was held by Kiev

keyframe_review.note: 19,978 km2. The page gives no area ('Area: not given'), so no ratio can be taken; it places the principality 'on a three way stick between Vitebsk, Minsk and Mogilev regions', which fits the bbox (53.2-55.1N, 28.5-30.8E). The shape is unchanged but its years are not: 'In 1116, the Principality of Drutsk was taken over by the Grand Principality of Kiev' and the page's list of princes has no Drutsk prince between Boris (to 1119) and Rogvolod II (from 1140). Cliopatria draws it continuously.
19,892 km2 for 1188-1201; a grid-level change (-85 km2) no page explains. The page's 12th-century princes (Boris 'until 1196') give no frontier.
19,977 km2 for 1202-1240; same shape as 1111. The page names Vojtech of Drutsk about 1217 and nothing else for the period.
19,834 km2 for 1241-1249. The page gives no Mongol-period events for Drutsk; Cliopatria's row ends in 1249.

correction.text: the 1241-1249 shape carried forward until Minsk takes Drutsk over in the second half of the 13th century

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, confidence 1: Cliopatria's Drutsk row ends in 1249 and its Minsk row absorbs the land in 1260. The page says Drutsk was 'entirely taken over by the Principality of Minsk' in the second half of the 13th century, giving no year, so the shape is bridged to the year before Cliopatria's Minsk shape grows.

ledger.note: 1101: Drutsk becomes a principality under Rogvolod-Boris when Polotsk is divided. 'established after the death of Vseslav, the Prince of Polotsk, in 1101'; 'Drutsk was given to Rogvolod-Boris when Vseslav's Polotsk territory was divided among his sons'. The page gives the location only as between the Vitebsk, Minsk and Mogilev regions; the region is Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: the Principality of Drutsk, 'taken over by the Grand Principality of Kiev'

ledger.note: 1116: Vladimir Monomakh's Kiev takes over Drutsk. 'In 1116, the Principality of Drutsk was taken over by the Grand Principality of Kiev.' The Minsk page has Monomakh's war on Minsk in the same year (1116).

region.text: Drutsk, back under a prince of the Polotsk line

ledger.note: 1140: Drutsk is again ruled by its own princes. The page says that 'by 1150s it was returned to Principality of Minsk' (and lists Gleb, son of Rostislav of Minsk, from 1151) but its list of princes resumes in 1140 with Rogvolod II of Polotsk (1140-1146), after a gap from 1119; the Vitebsk page has the exiled Polotsk princes allowed to return in 1139. The year is the list's and the return may be earlier.

region.text: Drutsk, 'entirely taken over by the Principality of Minsk'

ledger.note: Second half of the 13th century: Minsk absorbs Drutsk. 'Drutsk was entirely taken over by the Principality of Minsk.' The page gives no year; 1259 is the year before Cliopatria's enlarged Minsk shape (1260) and is the researcher's bridging.
The Principality of Drutsk ends in Minsk's. The page's later history (Vitebsk in the early 14th century, Lithuanian autonomy, Orsha county in 1565-1566) is not drawn.

wars.name: Kievan takeover of Drutsk (1116)
wars.outcome: The Principality of Drutsk was taken over by the Grand Principality of Kiev in 1116 and had princes of the Polotsk line again from 1140.
wars.note: The Minsk page puts Monomakh's war on Gleb of Minsk, with a siege of Minsk, in 1116. The Drutsk page gives no battle.

wars.name: Quarrel over Polotsk (1162)
wars.outcome: 'the princes of Vitebsk, Minsk and Drutsk began to quarrel over the control of Polotsk' in 1162; no territorial result on the page.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer can see it was considered.

certainty.note: The pages give a position 'between the Vitebsk, Minsk and Mogilev regions' and no frontier line.

notes: Pages opened: 5 of up to 5. Infobox area: none ('Area: not given'). START: the page and the Minsk page give 1101; Cliopatria opens in 1111 (a new 1101-1110 keyframe carries the shape back). END: Cliopatria ends in 1249 and has no row for 1250-1259; its Minsk shape from 1260 includes Drutsk, and the page says Minsk took Drutsk over 'in the second half of the 13th century', so the dossier bridges to 1259 at confidence 1 and hands over to principality-of-minsk. 1116-1139: the page says Kiev took Drutsk over in 1116 and the princes' list has no Drutsk prince from 1119 to 1140, so the land is Kiev's in the ledger though Cliopatria draws it continuously; the page itself contradicts this in two places (1140-1146 Rogvolod II 'of Polotzk', and 'returned to Principality of Minsk' by the 1150s, which names the 1151 prince Gleb, son of Rostislav of Minsk, as Drutsk's ruler). The Kievan Rus' dossier should carry the matching gain. The page's later history (Vitebsk control in the early 14th century, Algirdas, Orsha county 1565-1566) is outside the Cliopatria years. Gazetteer: 'Drutsk' (historic town in Belarus, near the Drut river in the Vitebsk-Minsk-Mogilev area) is needed; the capital point is a placeholder.
